title: Oxygen-rich medicine

controls.range_label: Comparison spans the sea-level enrichment threshold and the example chamber's rated maximum.

sources.label: NFPA 53 second draft report, annex A.3.3.25 discussion of NFPA 99

evidence.text: A review of reports from 1923 to 1996 counted 77 deaths in 35 hyperbaric chamber fires across Asia, Europe and North America.

sources.label: Sheffield and Desautels, 73-year chamber fire analysis, p. 153

evidence.text: NASA developed fine water mist for the ISS cabin because astronaut emergency breathing equipment could not filter carbon dioxide.

sources.label: NASA Spinoff (2020), Zero-Leak Valve Holds Tight in Demanding Environments

evidence.text: The hospital point marks a definition threshold, and the hyperbaric point shows the rated maximum of a specific monoplace chamber model.

sources.label: NFPA 53 second draft report, annex A.3.3.25 discussion of NFPA 99

gaps: The plotted NASA droplet and gas runs do not establish how cotton, silicone tubing or alcohol pads ignite at Earth gravity in wards, incubators or hyperbaric chambers.
The ISS extinguisher and breathing-equipment models illustrate spacecraft hardware. Hyperbaric systems have their own design and performance criteria.

source_quotes.text: While hyperbaric fire suppression systems are water-based, they have design and performance criteria different from other types of fire suppression systems.

sources.label: NFPA 99 hyperbaric first draft, first revision 953, annex A.14.3.4.3.7

title: Smoke in low-ventilation spaces

evidence.text: In SAME, a substantial share of the smoke particles from the materials tested measured below 500 nm across. The study’s transport model found that mixing dominated smoke movement in microgravity.

sources.label: Yang et al., SAME NASA technical memorandum, abstract

evidence.text: NASA identified false alarms during maintenance, such as vacuuming, as a reason crews sometimes disable alarms.

sources.label: Ruff, NASA spacecraft fire safety technology, 2021

evidence.text: NASA flame-spread work varied airflow, pressure and oxygen to study which combinations sustained spread in the materials tested.

sources.label: Olson et al., Microgravity Flame Spread in Exploration Atmospheres

evidence.text: The Shuttle-era Brunswick detector distinguished dust from combustion particles, a useful comparison for nuisance alarms in mines, submarines and server rooms.

gaps: On Earth, buoyancy can carry warm smoke upward even when mechanical ventilation is off. Detector placement and alarm times require evidence from the actual space.
The map does not estimate smoke paths, alarm coverage or room-specific ventilation effects.

title: Aircraft cabin and cargo hold

evidence.text: The cabin map point uses standard-atmosphere pressure at the FAA’s 8,000-foot normal cabin-altitude limit and the oxygen fraction of dry air.

sources.label: U.S. Standard Atmosphere (1976), lower-atmosphere pressure model
NASA atmospheric effects reference, dry air composition

evidence.text: NASA reports that a detector tracking particles and chemical species performed better than the aircraft smoke detectors used for comparison in joint NASA–FAA tests of false-alarm rejection and real-event detection.

sources.label: NASA Researcher’s Guide to Combustion Science, p. 35

gaps: Nearby droplet or gas runs compare oxygen and pressure. Cabin altitude does not set atmospheric conditions in every cargo hold.
NASA microgravity runs near the cabin point cannot establish how fast cargo materials burn or how detectors perform in an individual aircraft.

title: Battery fires

evidence.text: NASA developed a lithium-ion battery fire test as part of qualifying the ISS fine-water-mist extinguisher.

sources.label: NASA portable extinguisher qualification and lithium-ion fire test methods

gaps: The EMBER PSI combustion inventory contains no battery-fire runs.
A future investigation would need comparable cell types, charge states, pack layouts, airflow and ignition conditions, with measurements of heat release, cell-to-cell spread and reignition.
